verdicts.title: Partial matching width and its application to lower bounds for branching programs
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We introduce a new structural graph parameter called \emph{partial matching width}. For each (sufficiently large) integer $k \geq 1$, we introduce a class $\mathcal{G}_k$ of graphs of treewidth at most $k$ and max-degree $7$ such that for each $G \in \mathcal{G}_k$ and each (sufficiently large) $V \subseteq V(G)$, the partial matching width of $V$ is $Ω(k \log |V|)$.
  We use the above lower bound to establish a lower bound on the size of non-deterministic read-once branching programs (NROBPs).
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns 'partial matching width' and lower bounds for non-deterministic read-once branching programs on bounded-treewidth CNFs, which shares the BP lower-bound framework but does not address Lie nilpotency class, layer-algebra commutators, read-twice BPs, or IP_2.

verdicts.title: Hom 3-Lie-Rinehart Algebras
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
After endowing with a 3-Lie-Rinehart structure on Hom 3-Lie algebras, we obtain a class of special
  Hom 3-Lie algebras, which have close relationships with representations of commutative associative algebras. We provide a special class of Hom 3-Lie-Rinehart algebras, called split regular Hom 3-Lie-Rinehart algebras, and we then characterize their structures by means of root systems and weight systems associated to a splitting Cartan subalgebra.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Hom 3-Lie-Rinehart algebras, root systems, and splitting Cartan subalgebras — a structural Lie-theoretic topic with no mention of nilpotency class, branching programs, or IP_2 lower bounds.
